Indian Standard 

METHODS OF TEST FOR 
PETROLEUM AND ITS PRODUCTS : 

[P : 78] 

DETERMINATION OF TRACE ELEMENTS IN 
PETROLEUM PRODUCTS — COPPER 

(Incorporating Amendment No. 1) 

UDC 662.753.12 [621.438] : 629.13 : 543 : 546.56 

Adapted from IP 225/76 Copper in Aviation Turbine Fuels and 
Light Petroleum Distillates 

1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard describes a method for the determination of copper from 250 
/ig/kg down to about 10 /ig/kg (see Note) in aviation turbine fuels and 
petroleum distillates of similar boiling range. 

NOTE — This lower limit may not be achieved in a contaminated atmosphere unless 
special precautions are taken. 

2. OUTLINE OF THE METHOD 

2.1 The sample is treated with sodium hypochlorite solution and the copper 
extracted by washing with hydrochloric acid. Ammonium citrate and EDTA 
(disodium salt of ethylene diamine tetra-acetic acid) are used to eliminate 
interferences, and the copper is complexed with sodium 
diethyldithiocarbamate. The coloured complex is extracted with chloroform 
and the copper estimated by measuring the colour intensity on a 
spect rophot ometer . 

3. APPARATUS 

3.1 Spectrophotometer - capable of measuring light absorption at 435 nm. 

3.2 Separating Funnels — 100, 250 and 500 ml capacity ( see IS : 
1575-1960*). 



* Specification for separating funnels.

IS : 1448 [P : 78] - 1973 

3.3 Graduated Cylinders — 10, 25 and 250 ml capacity ( see IS : 878-1956* ). 

3.4 Pipettes — 10 ml capacity ( see IS : 4162-1967t ). 

3.5 Glass Funnels — ( see IS : 1541-1959* ). 

3.6 Glass Stoppered Flasks — 10 ml capacity ( see IS : 1590-1960§ ). 

3.7 Sample Container — a suitable, clear glass bottle, approximately 200 ml 
capacity, fitted with a glass stopper. Preferably new bottles should be used. 

Note -— It has been found that some samples deteriorate on standing, precipitating 
copper on the walls of the container. To account for this, steps are taken in the 
procedure to acid extract the bottles and to add the extract to the solution for 
analysis. For this reason, it is important to use bottles of the right size for sampling 
to bring the total quantity of copper within the desired range for determination. 

All sampling bottles should be clean and dry. If necessary they may be rinsed with 
the hypochlorite solution and the hydrochloric acid stipulated in 4.2 and 4.3. Used 
bottles shall not be used when samples of low copper content are expected. 

4. REAGENTS 

4.0 Quality of the Reagents — Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals 
and distilled water ( see IS : 1070-1960 1 1 ) shall be used in tests. 

NOTE — 'Pure chemicals' shall mean chemicals that do not contain impurities which 
affect the results of analysis. 

4.1 Distilled Water — copper content not to exceed 20 pg/litre. This is 
required for the preparation of the reagent solutions and for use in the test 
procedure. 

4.2 Sodium Hypochlorite — approximately 5 percent mass available 
chlorine solution. This shall be checked by the classical iodine-starch titration 
procedure. 

4.3 Hydrochloric Acid — approximately 4 N. 

4.4 EDTA (Disodium Salt) Solution, Aqueous — 5 percent ( m/v). 

4.5 Ammonium Citrate Solution, Aqueous — 10 percent ( m/v). 

4.6 Ammonium Hydroxide — - relative density 0.88. 

4.7 Chloroform 

4.8 Sodium Diethyldithiocarbamate Solution — one percent ( /n/v), 
prepared daily and filtered. 

4.9 Sodium Sulphate, Anhydrous — powder. 



* Specification for graduated measuring cylinders, 
t Specification for graduated pipettes. 
^Specification for glass filter funnels. 
§Specification for glass filter flasks.

IS : 1448 [P : 78] - 1973 

4.10 Standard Copper Sulphate Solution — (5 yg Cu per ml) prepared 
from clear crystals (that is, showing no efflorescence) of copper sulphate 
(CuS0 4 .5H 2 0) as follows: 

Dissolve 0.393 g of copper sulphate in distilled water. Add 5 ml of 
concentrated hydrochloric acid and dilute to 1 litre with the distilled water. 
Pipette 5 ml of this solution and dilute to 100 ml with distilled water. This 
gives a standard solution containing 5 /ig of Cu in 1 ml of water. 

4.11 Acetone 

5. PREPARATION OF APPARATUS 

5.1 It is desirable to have a set of glassware which is used only for these 
analyses (see Note). New glassware should be cleaned with concentrated 
hydrochloric acid and washed with distilled water. When necessary use a 
small quantity of acetone and a vacuum line for drying glassware. 

Note — Stopcock grease is often a source of contamination. Lubricate separating 
funnel stopcocks with poly tetrafluoro ethylene (PTFE) aerosol spray or employ 
PTFE taps. 

6. PROCEDURE 

6.1 Preparation of Calibration Graph — Add 0, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0, 6.0 and 8.0 ml 
portions of the 5 //g/ml standard copper sulphate solution to a series of 100-ml 
separating funnels and then add 8 ml of the hydrochloric acid and 15 ml of the 
ammonium hydroxide, mixing well with frequent venting after each addition. 
Add 2 ml of the sodium diethyldithiocarbamate solution to each separating 
funnel, mix, and allow 3 minutes for the yellow coloured complex to develop. 
Add exactly 10 ml of the chloroform to each separating funnel and extract by 
shaking vigorously for 2 minutes. Collect each chloroform extract in a 
glass-stoppered flask containing a little sodium sulphate (approximately 25 
mg). 

6.1.1 Measure the absorbance at 435 nm of each chloroform extract in a 1-cm 
cell using chloroform as the reference solution (also determine the correction 
values for each cell used, if matched cells are not available). Plot the corrected 
absorbance values against yg copper (per 10 ml of chloroform solution). 

6.2 Analysis of Sample 

6.2.1 Take samples for analysis in the special bottles prescribed in 3.7. 

6.2.2 Run a blank omitting the sample. 

6.2.3 Weigh the bottle and sample to the nearest 1.0 g. Pour the sample into a 
250-ml separating funnel and allow the sample bottle to drain. Re-weigh the 
bottle and determine the mass of sample. Add 10 ml of the sodium hypochlorite 
solution to the bottle and swirl for 1 minute so that it washes all the interior 
surface. Pour the hypochlorite solution from the bottle into the separating 
funnel. Shake the separating funnel vigorously for 2 minutes with frequent 
venting. Add 10 ml of the hydrochloric acid to the bottle and swirl as before. 
Pour the hydrochloric acid from the bottle into the separating funnel and 
shake for a further period of 2 minutes. Run the aqueous extract into a 100-ml 



IS : 1448 [P : 78] - 1973 

separating funnel. Repeat washing procedure with 5 ml of hydrochloric acid, 
and then 10 ml of water. Add the washings to the 100-ml separating funnel. 

6.2.4 Add 5 ml of the ammonium citrate solution and 5 ml of the EDTA 
solution to the aqueous phase and mix. Finally add 15 ml of the ammonium 
hydroxide and mix again. (CAUTION — Add ammonium hydroxide slowly, 
particularly to the blank.) 

6.2.5 Wash the ammoniacal extract with 20 ml aliquots of chloroform until the 
chloroform has a very low optical density at 435 nm. Three washings are 
normally adequate. Finally allow layers to separate completely and drain off 
as much chloroform as possible. Discard washings. 

6.2.6 Pipette 10 ml of the sodium diethyldithiocarbamate solution into the 
ammoniacal extract, shake and allow to stand for 3 minutes to enable the 
yellow coloured complex to develop. Add exactly 10 ml of chloroform, shake 
vigorously for 2 minutes, and allow the layers to separate. 

6.2.7 Run the chloroform layer into a glass-stoppered flask containing a small 
quantity of sodium sulphate. 

6.2.8 Shake the flask and allow the phases to separate. Within 20 minutes 
measure the absorbance of the chloroform extract at 435 nm in a 1-cm cell, 
using chloroform as a reference. 

NOTE — if preferred 300 ml of the sample may be used. In this case use 25 ml of 
chloroform for the final extraction of the coloured complex. This would permit the use 
of 4-cm cells for measuring the absorbance. A calibration graph representing /ig 
copper in 25 ml chloroform against the absorbance measured in 4-cm cells should be 
plotted. 

7. CALCULATION AND REPORTING 

7.1 Calculation — Calculate the copper content by the following formula: 

Copper content, fJg/kg = ~- — 

where 

A = copper in pg in sample — copper in //g in blank, and 
M= mass in g of the sample. 

7.2 Reporting — Report the result as copper content in /Jg/kg. 

8. PRECISION 

8.1 Repeatability — Duplicate test results shall not differ by more than 
20jig/kg. 

8.2 Reproducibility — The reproducibility of the method has not yet been 
established. 

EXPLANATORY NOTE

modification of the text as the result of incorporation of the amendment.
